extracted.intended_audience: United Way marketing/communications staff, local United Way offices, vendors and designers producing United Way materials
extracted.subtask_description: Brand standards and usage rules for United Way visual and verbal identity, covering logo/lockup use, color, typography, photography, messaging tone, naming/localization, advertising layouts, file naming, and brand architecture. Intended to ensure consistent, legally-protected, and on-brand communications across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / correct and consistent implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines are provided to ensure the correct and consistent use of the brand identity system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By accurately and consistently implementing the brand identity system (voice, brandmark, typography, color palette, visual elements), you protect the equity of the United Way brand and strengthen brand positioning. Use the directions included to help manage communication materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand framework components
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand framework includes Vision, Mission, Brand Promise, Brand Positioning, and Brand Idea as foundational statements that guide communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vision: long-term aspirational outcome. Mission: how the organization will achieve the vision. Brand Promise: what drives the brand's unique promise. Brand Positioning: how the brand drives value and should be communicated. Brand Idea: singular motivating idea ('To live better, we must LIVE UNITED'). Use these to orient messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two sides of United Way (Fight vs Win communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating communications, determine whether the piece is about the problem ('UNITED WE FIGHT') or the solution ('UNITED WE WIN').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces about the fight should be bold, direct, and serve as a rally cry to inspire action. Pieces about the win should be celebratory, uplifting and bright, focusing on successes and congratulating participants. Visual elements (color tone, imagery) differ between the two and must follow the corresponding 'fight' or 'win' palettes and photography styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand tone — strength and action orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand communications must have a tone of strength: uplifting, empowering, motivating, and inspiring action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should be thoughtful and matter-of-fact, challenging, confident, and trustworthy. Avoid clichés, passive language and muddying the message with complexities. Always ask: Is this message honest? Is it clear? Does it inspire emotion and action?

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice style — personification and allowed/disallowed traits
rubrics_metrics.description: How United Way 'sounds'—the brand personification and adjectives that describe appropriate voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNITED WAY IS: honest, optimistic, purposeful, credible, encouraging, empathetic, inclusive, human. UNITED WAY IS NOT: fabricated, ungrateful, vague, passive, exclusive, disrespectful, stuffy, careless. Use these as heuristics when writing; avoid vague requests and undefined causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local messaging phrasing ('We're Local' and 'LIVE UNITED against')
rubrics_metrics.description: Localize messaging to the community using the phrasing 'LIVE UNITED against' where possible; alternatives are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred: 'In Milwaukee, we LIVE UNITED AGAINST TEEN PREGNANCY.' Circumstantially acceptable: 'In Milwaukee, we fight for the health of teens.' Incorrect: 'In Milwaukee, we fight against teen pregnancy.' Maintain positive call to action; avoid 'fight against' where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices: capitalization, punctuation, grammar, brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific short rules for copy mechanics and tone economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines should be entirely capitalized. Subheads should live as the first sentence of body copy and be bolded if used. Include punctuation in headlines and at the end of complete sentences; avoid exclamation points except very sparingly and never in headlines. For grammar not covered here, refer to the Chicago Manual of Style. Keep messages concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of 'United'
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'United' should be capitalized when used in any written context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: 'The group United to bring new opportunities...' and 'We win by living United.' Treat 'United' as a brand tribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brandmark fundamental rule (do not alter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The United Way brandmark is the primary visual element and must appear only as shown or in approved variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never redraw, rescale, extract elements, add graphic elements, or display elements separately. Always display the registered trademark symbol (®) in the indicated position. The brandmark's components communicate caring, inspiring, trustworthy and approachable attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo usage: full-color primary and color modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-color version is the primary brandmark and required whenever possible; Pantone spot color preferred; CMYK and RGB available for application requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Pantone spot for print (preferred). For on-screen uses, use the RGB file. Never replace full-color where it's usable with one-color variants. Always use the brandmark exactly as provided and in approved color builds (see color palette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control box usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The white control box is a border that surrounds the logo used to create separation on colored backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use control box to keep logo legible when placed on colored backgrounds without needing alternate logo colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-color and special-usage logo rules
rubrics_metrics.description: One-color versions are allowed when reproduction constraints exist; special usage lock-ups are allowed for certain materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-color blue and black may be used only when those are the only available color options. Special-usage lock-ups (black, white, United Way Blue) are permitted for fabric, plastic, glass, merchandise, and signage and do not require the white control box. Do not use special or one-color lock-ups on websites or four-color brochures where full-color is usable. One-color marks may not be reproduced in colors other than those specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear space and minimum size
rubrics_metrics.description: Logo must be surrounded by minimum clear space and must not be reproduced below minimum sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear space is determined by 1/2 the height of the symbol square. Minimum sizes: Screen: 90 pixels or 1.25" wide; Print minimum size: .75" wide; Special usage minimum: .75" wide. Maintain specified clear space from other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable brandmark uses (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated prohibited alterations of the brandmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never: use LIVE UNITED as part of the brandmark lockup; tilt; distort; alter colors; rearrange elements; change the shape; add elements inside the brandmark; substitute type inside the brandmark; put other words/phrases inside; change the font or color of 'United Way' contained in the brandmark; extract graphic elements to use separately. Follow examples and never attempt to redraw or rescale the brandmark or local identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Artwork files follow a specific naming convention to identify contents quickly; file names consist of lowercase letters with underscores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts of the filename denote Company (united-way-lockup), Color (cmyk, spot, spot-3, rgb, blue, black, white), Version (spot, special), and Format suffix (eps). All logos are also available in JPEG. Use .eps high-resolution vector art to create other formats. Follow the documented examples (e.g., united-way-lockup-cmyk.eps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork and file format guidance (which file to use when)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which logo file to use for printing, web, video, and special reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cmyk.eps for four-color process printing and documents with full-color photos. Use spot (spot.eps) for spot color printing (silk-screened items like T-shirts). Use spot-3 for three-color spot printing. Use rgb.eps for video, PowerPoint and web; DO NOT use RGB files for printing. Use one-color spot file when United Way Blue is the only color available. Use special usage files when screening of inks is not possible (plastic, glass, metal, fabric). Use white special for dark backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming convention for local identifiers (typography and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local identifier (location name) always appears first upper case then all lower case Roboto Bold and has prescribed placement options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local identifier must appear as shown in variations; never redraw or rescale the local identifier relative to the brandmark. Follow color, placement, size specs; vertical lockup suits vertical formats; the local identifier can be up to three lines in vertical lockup and may be decreased slightly if it exceeds width by 2–3 letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions worldwide / United States (ordering rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized preferred arrangements for naming United Way entities across tiers (countries, cities, regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier guidance: Tier 1 (Worldwide Brands/Countries) prefer 'United Way' then 'Country Name', or 'United Way of [Country]'. Tier 2 (International city-based offices) prefer 'United Way of [City]'. Tier 3 (U.S. regional/city-based) preferred 'United Way of [City]' for cities; region names prefer '[Region] United Way' or 'United Way of [Region]'. Follow provided examples for preferred/second arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brandmark localization (lockup proportions and default positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred local master brand lockups and their default positions (left, vertical, under lockup) with precise proportional relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left-of-lockup is preferred; vertical lockup for vertical formats; localizations are primary signatures for local communications unless unsuitable. Maintain exact proportional relationships (1/3, 1/2 unit spacing, etc.) and minimum clearance (1/2 square). Local identifier position is fixed relative to holding shape; on colored backgrounds expand control line to hold identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media brandmarks (symbol usage for small screens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the United Way symbol (square or circle) for social profile images to improve legibility on mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Square mark for platforms that display square profile pics (Facebook, Twitter); circle mark for platforms with circular display (Instagram, Pinterest). Follow correct/incorrect examples to ensure legibility and proper composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIVE UNITED tagline usage and clearspace
rubrics_metrics.description: 'LIVE UNITED' is a closing tagline and must be used in specific ways and in combination with the brandmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tagline as closing to headlines and key statements. For 'UNITED WE FIGHT' use orange tagline lockup; for 'UNITED WE WIN' use yellow lockup. The tagline should never appear on its own and must always be accompanied by the United Way logo. It must not be placed within 2 vertical, 2 horizontal, or 1 diagonal unit of the logo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action: 'GIVE. ADVOCATE. VOLUNTEER.' usage constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard CTA to be used on United Way marketing communications with restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 'GIVE. ADVOCATE. VOLUNTEER.' on marketing communications including advertising and collateral. Do NOT use it in cause-related communications or communications involving multiple partners, nor on premium items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color palette and application (general / fight / win palettes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary color palette derived from the brandmark with additional colors for flexibility; separate palettes for 'general', 'UNITED WE FIGHT', and 'UNITED WE WIN'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colors consistently across media to strengthen recognition. Primary palette comprises Pantone 287, 659, 179, 143 plus black, orange, grey, white. Use the 'fight' palette (darker/desaturated; highlights seriousness) only in fight layouts; 'win' palette (light, bright) only in win layouts; general palette for neutral pieces. Refer to CMYK, RGB, and HEX specs and note that on-page colors may not match Pantone standards—refer to Pantone standards for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography: approved typefaces and substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Three standardized typefaces: League Gothic (headline), Roboto (body), Roboto Condensed Bold (headings), with Arial as an acceptable substitute under constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use specified weights and styles shown. Trade Gothic and Meta discontinued. Roboto family may be used for extended weights in special circumstances. Arial may substitute for Roboto when Roboto is unavailable and may be used in correspondence, word-processed documents, PowerPoint, and narrative text on websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography usage: size, tracking, line spacing, hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using headline, heading, subhead, and body fonts, including relative sizes and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines: League Gothic, used sparingly; use block behind text if legibility issue. Headings: Roboto Condensed Bold with specified tracking and line spacing (e.g., -10 tracking; 1.1–1.3X line spacing). Subheads: Roboto Bold as first sentence of paragraph. Body copy: Roboto Regular with recommended sizes (8–14 pt) and 1.5–2X line spacing. Headline tracking examples given (25 tracking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography style guidelines (journalistic, fight vs win)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography must be journalistic and authentic; style differs for 'Fight' (desaturated) and 'Win' (colorful, positive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images that make you feel something and place you in the environment. When using multiple photos in a composition, include a blend of perspectives (close up, mid range, far away/landscape). 'UNITED WE FIGHT' images: showcase challenges, heavily desaturated but not black-and-white. 'UNITED WE WIN' images: colorful, positive, feature faces of those experiencing the reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconography rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Icons should maintain consistent look, use United Way brand colors, and prefer circle shapes with specified internal proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating icons, prefer circle shapes. Follow the specified proportions (2% inner margins, 8% offsets, 80% central area, etc.) and use only brand colors. Examples provided for Email, News, Events icons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps & graphics styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics and charts should maintain consistent look, use brand colors and favor circle shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brand colors only. Circle shapes preferred for graphic elements and charts. Maintain consistent look and feel with iconography rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print ad composition — 'UNITED WE FIGHT' and 'UNITED WE WIN' print ad rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Print ads composed of six key components with different color and tone rules for fight vs win.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components: 1) Images per photo guidelines. 2) Headline (white text on black for fight; white on blue for win) with messaging tone matching fight/win. 3) LIVE UNITED logo follows headline (white text on orange for fight; white on yellow for win). 4) Additional details in body copy; subhead as first sentence bolded. 5) Include 'Give. Advocate. Volunteer.' on all print pieces. 6) United Way logo in lower right as signature. Follow layout diagrams and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print ad layout formula (proportions and margins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for logo size, headline size relative to logo, margins and placement of Live United and CTA in print ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logo size ranges between 5 and 7 widths of the brandmark (1–3 widths when medium <4"). Headlines should be 50–75% the height of the United Way logo and at least 1.5X larger than Live United copy. Blocks around type should be 1/4 square margin. LIVE UNITED attached directly under headline. Headline and LIVE UNITED must remain left-aligned and cannot come within 1 square margin of body copy. CTA should be last line in body copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting to smaller ad sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: When reducing ad size, allowable reductions to margins and copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable to reduce white frame from 1 square to 1/2 on half page layouts and 1/3 on quarter page layouts. Reduce copy as necessary to maintain hierarchy and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital display ad components
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital ads have five key components mirroring print guidelines with digital-specific placement advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Images per photo guidelines. 2) Headline color/treatment as in print. 3) LIVE UNITED tagline follows headline as in print. 4) Clear CTA directing next step (e.g., 'Hear his story', 'Give. Advocate. Volunteer', 'Join the fight'). 5) United Way logo as signature in lower right (or top left if height is an issue). Ensure on-screen legibility and use RGB/web files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billboard composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Billboards must align with fight or win objectives and follow specific logo and CTA placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow color/design formats for 'UNITED WE FIGHT' or 'UNITED WE WIN'. United Way logo should appear in white space to the left of the board with 'GIVE. ADVOCATE. VOLUNTEER.' below. Use bold, high-contrast headlines suitable for roadside legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video, animation, and interactive guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen-based media should follow print guidelines but allow limited exceptions due to dynamic nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brandmark, preferred placement, brand color palette, typography and impact graphic. Full-color brandmark is the only version for screen applications. Preferred placement is right side but may be centered if technically or aesthetically necessary. Use League Gothic for impact text and the brand palette for colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior and interior signage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Signage must use the white background control box; metal sign exceptions allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exterior signage must use white background control box around brandmark. Interior full-color signs must also use the white control box; metal signs may be made of one metal type and do not need the control outline. Use signage examples as design intent; final fabrication and measurements determined with vendor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand architecture levels and visual rules (Levels 1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic approach to ordering relationships between corporate, member and offer brands using Levels 1–5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 1: United Way masterbrand only. Level 2A: Affinity group identities (masterbrand dominant, controlled by United Way, not standalone). Level 2B: Product & event identities (stand-alone identities controlled by United Way). Level 3: Partner dominant with United Way endorsement (mutual affiliation; partner visual dominant). Level 4: Legacy brands (historical/legal constraints; retain identity where needed). Level 5: Partnerships and co-sponsorships (partner logos center-aligned, spaced equally; United Way brandmark appears last/farthest right or bottom). Apply color/treatment rules per level and follow provided visualizations and proportional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy brands handling (Level 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: When existing identities have history/equity/legal constraints, retain them but incorporate United Way elements where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type and color should be changed to conform to guidelines wherever possible. Refer to specific logo usage guidelines for legacy marks. Retire previously used logos where required, but repurpose any artwork that does not include the old name if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership/co-sponsorship visualization rules (Level 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for arranging partner and co-sponsor logos and the United Way mark in cooperative efforts where United Way is lead partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner logos should be center-aligned, spaced equally and optically at same size. United Way brandmark should appear last and farthest right/bottom. Examples provided for horizontal and vertical co-sponsorship arrangements. If United Way is not lead, guidelines may be recommended but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: System overview / application development principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand elements are building blocks for all communications; follow guidelines to meet brand objectives while allowing creative flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identity elements (brandmark, color, typography, taglines, photography) as prescribed to maintain brand positioning and consistency. Apply 'general', 'fight', and 'win' color hierarchies appropriately. Find tools and resources on the Brand Management Website and contact United Way Worldwide Marketing for questions.
